newsitem.title: GERMANY: Russian demand boosts German confectionery exports.
newsitem.headline: Russian demand boosts German confectionery exports.

text.p: German confectionery exports should rise further in 1997 after increasing in 1996 due to sharply higher sales to Russia and eastern Europe, export promotion body German Sweets said in a statement.
"The year 1996 was quite significant and it looks as if we might increase sales again this year," said chairman Ruediger Larssen.
Of the 306,000 tonnes of third country exports in 1996 (263,000 tonnes in 1995), some 200,000 went to central and eastern European countries, German Sweets said.
Russia accounted for 128,000 tonnes, which represented a 37 percent increase over 1995.
Of the Russian total, 77,000 tonnes were chocolate products (up 20 percent), 34,000 tonnes cocoa-containing foods (up 110 percent) and 2,000 tonnes semi-finished cocoa products (up 20 percent).
Some 4,000 tonnes were boiled sweets (up 55 percent), 6,000 tonnes biscuits (plus 89 percent), 1,650 tonnes savoury snacks (minus 24 percent) and 3,000 tonnes ice cream (minus one).
Eastern Europe, including other CIS states, accounted for 71,000 tonnes (up 27 percent), with Ukraine raising its imports to 15,000 tonnes from 4,000 a year earlier.
Germany also sold 571,000 tonnes to other European Union countries in 1996, 7,000 tonnes more than in 1995.
Total German output in 1996 was 3.14 million tonnes, of which 28 percent was exported and earned four billion marks (up three percent).
